transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10 | Start: 10:00 PST | Duration approx 45 min
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Patel, Jordan Reyes, Ava Thompson, Samir Gupta, Ellie Park, Noah Brooks, Priya Rao
Links shared: https://redwood.app/runbooks/platform-maintenance-v2 , drive: https://drive.redwood.com/ops/playbooks/maintenance-dryrun.xlsx

Summary (auto): Dry run of platform maintenance playbook focusing on KMS rotation, RBAC emergency access flow, billing chargeback notes, and audit evidence. Identified gaps in rollback steps and telemetry thresholds. Next steps and owners agreed.

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everybody thanks for joining on time uh this is the platform admin playbook dry-run, um we'll run through the steps like we would in a real maintenance window, call out any gaps, and make sure audit artifacts are captured.
[00:18] Liam Patel: yeah thanks maya. I can share my screen in a sec, um i put the latest playbook link in chat, it's the v2 doc - tiny changes from last week.
[00:25] Ellie Park: i got the link, opening now.
[00:30] Jordan Reyes: quick call out — i looked at the KMS rotation section and it references our key-policy but the sequence isn't explicit for the staging vs prod keys, so we might... uh risk a short outage if an operator picks the wrong key.
[00:45] Samir Gupta: ok that's exactly what we wanted to test, cause last quarter there was confusion during the cert rotation.
[00:52] Ava Thompson: add to that we need to capture the billing signal — like, if we do a 2-hour restart, what's the downstream chargeback to product teams, otherwise procurement will get angry.
[01:05] Maya Chen: right. For structure i propose we run by modules: pre-checks and comms, kms/key rotation, rbac and emergency access, service restart and cache warmup (kv cache was referenced as the kv-cache in the doc), telemetry checks, and post-run audit evidence. anyone want to change order?
[01:23] Noah Brooks: sounds good. Also we should validate log retention export as evidence for SOC two, uh SOC 2 — sometimes the speech-to-text tool writes it as 'sock too' in previous transcripts so.
[01:38] Priya Rao: (laughs) yes, please don't call it sock two in the audit repo.
[01:42] Liam Patel: ok i'll start with pre-checks, then we can role-play the ops steps. so pre-checks: confirm maintenance window, verify pager rotation, ensure backups for DBs (we have snapshot at 02:00 UTC), confirm KMS backup keys exist.
[01:56] Ellie Park: quick Q, snapshots are incremental - do we want a full backup? last time incremental plus a quick export worked but took an extra 20 min.
[02:10] Samir Gupta: minimal disruption is preferred, but if you need a 20-minute export add it to the timeline. The SRE team said they can hold a longer window if we give 48 hours notice.
[02:22] Jordan Reyes: stepping into KMS rotation — the playbook lists steps A-C, but not the verification step that services pick up the new key. we should add an automated verification: small write/read to a HA test secret after rotation with a timestamped log event.
[02:41] Liam Patel: good, we can run a 'kms-smoke' job — i have a script that does that but it's in a private gist. i'll drop it into the runbook.
[02:49] Maya Chen: note that as an action.
[02:52] [timestamp 03:00] Maya Chen: ok let's do a micro role-play — samir you're SRE lead, ellie you're oncall, jordan you're security, liam runs the steps, ava watches cost, and i'll narrate and script the comms. Go.
[03:12] Liam Patel: step 1: announce maintenance to #platform-notice, set statuspage to 'degraded' — i post now. (typing sounds) posted.
[03:25] Ellie Park: i see it. then i put the cluster into maintenance mode, cordon nodes, drain pods with disruption budgets in mind. um quick note the doc currently says 'kubectl drain' but not the --ignore-daemonsets flag, that bit is important.
[03:44] Jordan Reyes: and when you cordon the nodes — add a step to monitor long-running KV cache clients; we had one customer workload that relied on a sticky connection and it died mid-drain.
[03:58] Liam Patel: ack. the playbook calls it KV cache but transcribed different places as 'k v cache' — i'll normalize naming.
[04:10] [04:15] Samir Gupta: moving to KMS rotation — liam you simulate rotating the key now, step A: create new key version, step B: update alias to new version, step C: let services re-initialize.
[04:28] Liam Patel: creating new key version... (brief pause) created. updating alias... updated. services should start reloading per the agent.
[04:37] Ellie Park: i see a couple of services failing to reauth, service-auth-03 is throwing 401s.
[04:44] Jordan Reyes: that indicates some agents didn't pick up the new DEK — okay we need the verification step. Also capture the exact error codes for the audit log.
[04:55] Liam Patel: service-auth-03 shows stack trace, it fell back to cached key and timed out. i'll trigger a restart of the auth agent.
[05:05] Ellie Park: restarting now. (typing) restarted, auth agent connected, requests succeeding.
[05:15] Maya Chen: note: add explicit restart step in playbook after alias update, but pref it to be automated when possible.
[05:22] Noah Brooks: and add a telemetry threshold — e.g., if error rate > 1% for more than 2 minutes post-rotation, auto-rollback. otherwise operator notified.
[05:34] Jordan Reyes: yes, but auto-rollback needs a clear safe-state defined, because rolling back keys can be messy. the rollback procedure should include: re-alias previous key version, run smoke tests, and only then remove flag from statuspage.
[05:50] Ava Thompson: from cost side i want to flag the snapshot export — that incurred egress in Q4 for the staging region. add a note to pick the cheaper cross-region snapshot tier or schedule during low egress window.
[06:04] Liam Patel: good point. i'll add a cost note with links to the finops sheet.
[06:10] [06:20] Maya Chen: we're onto RBAC/emergency access. jordan?
[06:23] Jordan Reyes: emergency access flow is currently: 1) obtain approval token via SSO, 2) request temporary role elevation, 3) operator runs steps. The issue is the SSO approval sometimes times out and the operator stalls waiting. we should add an alternate path: short-lived service account with an approval ticket ID recorded in the audit log.
[06:45] Samir Gupta: can we make that a just-in-time elevation via the access broker? we tried it in sept but the broker's timeout is 3 minutes.
[06:55] Ellie Park: broker timeout is tunable, but for long ops we should request a 1-hour elevation window with enforced re-auth at 30 minutes.
[07:06] Jordan Reyes: agree. also document the RBAC step-by-step including CLI commands; the playbook currently links to the RBAC wiki but doesn't give copy-paste commands. that's where people make mistakes.
[07:20] Maya Chen: copy-paste commands + expected outputs, plus a troubleshooting appendix.
[07:25] [07:30] Liam Patel: moving to service restart and caching. the playbook uses 'warmup' steps for the kv-cache; we should also include sample traffic profiles for warmup like 100 rps for 5 minutes.
[07:41] Ellie Park: yes, and clear guidance on gradual traffic ramp to avoid 503 spikes. last time we saw a spike because we flipped the router too quickly.
[07:50] Noah Brooks: telemetry: what logs exactly do we need for SOC2 evidence? retention windows, export formats?
[07:58] Jordan Reyes: good Q. we need three things: 1) change control record (who did what and when), 2) system logs for the maintenance window (timestamped events), 3) exported access logs for any elevated sessions. i will map exact log filenames in the runbook.
[08:14] Ava Thompson: and please include the cost tag on those exports so finops can attribute storage/egress.
[08:20] Maya Chen: ok — we're at the part where we simulate a failure and exercise rollback. Liam, can you simulate the degraded telemetry?
[08:29] Liam Patel: sure, i'll flip the feature flag to force auth failures for service-auth-03. flipping now... (beep) looks like 401s rising to about 2.3%.
[08:42] Ellie Park: i'm seeing the spike. per playbook threshold >1% for 2 minutes triggers auto-rollback, correct?
[08:51] Jordan Reyes: yes but remind me if auto-rollback is enabled by default or operator opt-in. the doc says operator opt-in but maybe we want it on for critical services.
[09:02] Maya Chen: conversation — tradeoffs: auto-rollback reduces outage impact but may hide root causes and cause flip-flops. we should enable it for auth and payment pipelines but operator manual for non-critical infra.
[09:16] Samir Gupta: agreed. mark auth and billing as auto-rollback enabled.
[09:22] [09:30] Liam Patel: initiating rollback sequence — re-aliasing to previous key version... done. running kms-smoke job... smoke shows successes.
[09:42] Ellie Park: services returning to normal. spike ending.
[09:45] Noah Brooks: capture the rollback timeline in the change control record — we need to show time-to-detect and time-to-rollback for the audit.
[09:52] Jordan Reyes: logging note: the runbook should instruct operators to attach the smoke job output and the alias-change operation IDs to the change ticket.
[10:02] Ava Thompson: cost callout: if rollback triggers multiple rekeys in a short span, there is a marginal cost for key ops in our KMS billing. put an estimate in playbook.
[10:15] Maya Chen: ok, now let's exercise the post-run checklist — verify service health, export logs, update statuspage, and send closure comms. who wants to read the close comms template aloud?
[10:25] Priya Rao: i can read it. (reads) 'Maintenance window completed at 10:12 PST. Services validated. Please contact platform-support if you see degradation.' maybe add contact by role next time.
[10:36] Maya Chen: yes add SRE oncall and security mailing list.
[10:40] [10:45] Liam Patel: i want to call out one more operational gap: playbook references an internal runbook id 'PR-834' but we moved to new numbering and this causes lookup delays. we need canonical links not ids.
[10:57] Ellie Park: +1, canonical deep links, and retain copies in the runbook repo as attachments so ephemeral wiki edits don't break procedures.
[11:06] Jordan Reyes: documentation: include expected SLO impacts in the playbook; for instance 'latency may increase 10-30% for 15 minutes' and the mitigation steps. it helps product teams triage.
[11:20] Maya Chen: this has been great. let's wrap with explicit next steps and owners. (recap) Liam will update the playbook with: explicit verification step after KMS alias update, add restart instruction, normalize naming (kv-cache -> KV cache), embed kms-smoke script, and canonical deep links. Jordan will map audit log filenames and attach SOC2 evidence checklist. Ava will add cost notes and produce chargeback spreadsheet. Samir will confirm maintenance window with SRE.
[11:48] Priya Rao: one more tiny ask — please include procurement's standard wording for customer-facing maintenance notifications, we need legal-approved phrasing.
[11:58] Maya Chen: noted. i'll paste the procurement snippet into the comms template.
[12:05] [12:10] Noah Brooks: last minute: for the smoke verification step, can we add a SHA256 hash of a test payload in the log entry so auditors can validate we ran the same test?
[12:20] Jordan Reyes: yeah we can include the hash and the operation id.
[12:24] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after updates. Ending call.
